spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Measure a representative workload with `tracemalloc` or `sys.getsizeof`; `__slots__` does not automatically speed up an entire application.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: `__slots__` is not a security boundary and does not make objects immutable. Plan `__weakref__` and inheritance behavior explicitly.
PRACTICE EXAMPLE 2 · Using __slots__ to reduce object memory
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(slots=True)
class Point:
    x: float
    y: float

point = Point(3, 4)
print(point.x + point.y)

spans.title: Why it matters
spans.text: `__slots__` changes instance layout: it avoids an automatic per-instance `__dict__` and permits only declared attributes. This can help with many small objects, but verify the benefit by measuring. `dataclass(slots=True)` is a convenient option; account for dynamic attributes, weak references, and inheritance.
